meta_description: Fraud-and-error analytics on a benefits spine — overpayment recovery up 22% and underpayment corrections finding the people the system owed

blocks.x: Fraud-and-error analytics on a benefits spine — overpayment recovery up 22% and underpayment corrections finding the people the system owed

a social-security agency whose integrity program chased overpayments while underpayments — money the state owed its citizens — were found only by complaint. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline year measured the asymmetry: overpayment recovery at EUR 41M with error rates published, underpayment detection essentially reactive, and the agency's own auditors noting the integrity program measured only one direction of error.
Benefit, employment and income data lived apart; errors surfaced at review points. The citizen's experience of error correction was: notice it yourself, prove it yourself.

We built the benefits spine in both directions: employment, income and benefit events resolved to one entitlement model, error analytics running for over- and underpayment with the same rigor, correction queues ranked — underpayments fast-tracked to proactive repayment, overpayments routed to caseworkers with evidence — and outcome reporting published for both directions. Integrity became symmetric.
